summary: Patchwork is a light two-player abstract game where players buy irregularly-shaped tetromino-like patches to tile their personal 9x9 quilt board while managing a shared time track and limited buttons (currency). It's quick, tactile, and puzzly, with a satisfying tension between grabbing good pieces and staying ahead on time.
criticised: Limited long-term depth or replay variety
Can feel like a solved puzzle after many plays

interaction.kind: racing on a shared time track to grab pieces before the opponent can
interaction.detail: Only three patches are available to buy at any moment from a shared circle, and taking one advances your token on a shared time track, which can let you sneak extra turns before your opponent or take a patch you know they need. Even so, the actual quilt-building — the 9x9 grid each player fills — is entirely private and independent.
interaction.said: Often called a cozy, almost solitaire-feeling puzzle for two, but reviewers do note the sniping element — 'grabbing the piece your opponent obviously wanted' or 'jumping ahead on the time track to deny them a choice patch.'

sources: minus 2 points per empty square on your quilt board
+7 bonus for first to complete a 7x7 area
scoring.how_you_win: Buy patches to cover your board and generate button income; once both time tokens reach the end of the track, the player with more buttons (after penalties for holes) wins.
